answer: In PoA, each challenge task commits to a later threshold-BLS beacon pulse: its seed remains hidden until drand’s distributed quorum signs an unpredictable value, after which the task is derived by hashing that pulse with the agent commitment. A sybil swarm therefore cannot precompute solutions or farm identities offline; every attempt must await the future anchor, while commit-reveal checks expose equivocation. A knoll or ocean of cheap nodes gains no advantage because the beacon’s entropy is shared and unbiasable.
